newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bis shares likely to resume next Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Bis shares likely to resume next Tuesday.

text.p: Shares of French temporary help agency Bis are likely to start trading again next Tuesday after being suspended earlier this week following the death of company chairman Laurent Negro, a company official said on Thursday.
"It will likely be Tuesday," the official told Reuters by telephone when asked when trading in the stock would resume.
The shares in Bis SA were suspended last Monday at 533 francs a share following the death of Negro who founded the company, one of France's leading temporary employment agencies.
Negro's death has renewed market talk Bis could be the target of a takeover bid by a large foreign temporary help firm.
The family-controlled firm has appointed board member Claude Charbonniaud to succeed Negro. Bis has said he would "direct the group continuing the policies defined" by Negro last June.
That means, the Bis official said, that Bis would continue to seek an international partner. "This is an integral part (of our strategy)," he said. "It will followed in the same fashion."
The company signalled to analysts last year that a partnership would be sought through shareholder cross-holdings rather than an outright merger.

Asked whether this was still the case, the official said "things are a little different in that Negro's beneficiaries are not active in the business. It's a problem of capital. We need to find a solution to assure the future of Bis that also permits the family to preserve its interests."
The official said that the quest for an international ally was "more advanced than in June" but that it was premature to identify any potential partners.
At the June shareholders' meeting, Negro, who pioneered temporary help services in France, praised the merger last May between French manpower agency Ecco and Swiss personnel company Adia ADIA.Z.
Negro said Bis -- regarded by critics of being overly focused on France -- needed to "wake up" and take part in the fast-paced globalisation of the personnel services sector.

Negro said the family-controlled firm was searching for an international alliance "to satisfy multinational clients who reproach us for not being in New York or Tokyo" but did not identify any potential partners.

One possible partner cited by analysts earlier this week was U.S. temporary help giant Manpower but Manpower France was reported by French newspaper Liberation on Wednesday to have dismissed the idea. The company is known to favour more internal growth and franchising rather than acquisitions.
Other possible contenders for Bis which ranks third in France in market share behind Adecco and Manpower are the Netherlands' Randstad Holding NV and Vendex International NV and the U.S. Olsten Corp.
Adeco is seen an unlikely contender as it is still digesting the merger that spawned the company a year earlier.
Negro and his family held some 60 percent of the company which has 4,800 employees and a network of 500 agencies.
Bis, whose market capitalisation totals 2.5 billion francs, posted a first-half profit of 34 million francs, down from 70 million a year earlier.
It forecast 1996 full-year results would be sharply below the previous year's profit of 201 million francs, due to poor trading conditions and a one-off gain that boosted the 1995 results.
